risks.note: Manufacturing and supplying safe, effective and quality medicines is fundamental to the industry; any quality failure or product recall may result in regulatory action, product liability, business disruption and reputational damage, with negative implications including recalls, litigation, regulatory penalties and revenue loss. Mitigated through a Quality Management System, cGMP-compliant practices, validated processes, quality risk management, pharmacovigilance, traceability and internal audits.

The pharmaceutical industry operates under stringent national and international regulatory frameworks; non-compliance may delay product approvals, restrict market access and attract regulatory action, bringing compliance costs, penalties, product suspension and business interruptions. Dedicated Regulatory Affairs and Quality teams, periodic audits and SOPs are the stated mitigation.
risks.risk: Regulatory compliance across national and international frameworks

risks.note: Dependence on critical raw materials and global supply chains exposes the Company to supply disruptions, quality risks and ESG-related concerns, with increased procurement costs and disruptions from geopolitical or market uncertainties. Mitigated by quality audits, a Supplier Code of Conduct, periodic supplier evaluations, business continuity planning and supplier diversification.
risks.risk: Supply-chain dependence on critical raw materials and global sourcing

risks.note: Long-term success depends on attracting, developing and retaining skilled talent; talent shortages and high attrition may impact innovation and operational excellence, raising recruitment and training costs and causing productivity loss. Mitigated through structured learning and development, succession planning, leadership development, performance management and competitive remuneration.
risks.risk: Human capital development and talent retention

risks.note: Pharmaceutical manufacturing involves handling chemicals, biological materials and sophisticated equipment; workplace accidents may result in compensation claims, production loss and reputational impact. Mitigated by a structured EHS Management System covering hazard identification, risk assessment, safety audits, PPE compliance, behavioural safety, emergency preparedness and health surveillance.
risks.risk: Occupational health, safety and employee well-being

risks.note: Disruptions from natural disasters, pandemics, geopolitical events, utility failures, supply shortages or manufacturing interruptions may adversely affect production, distribution and availability of medicines, with potential revenue loss in prolonged disruptions. Mitigated through business continuity and disaster recovery measures including multiple manufacturing facilities, preventive maintenance, inventory planning, supplier diversification and periodic risk assessments.

Increased digitalisation exposes the Company to cybersecurity threats, operational disruptions and risks to confidential business and patient information, with potential financial losses, business interruption and reputational damage. Mitigated by layered controls including firewalls, endpoint protection, access controls, awareness programmes and periodic assessments.

The MD&A flags that companies operating in international markets face pricing pressures, changing reimbursement policies, patent expiries, rising regulatory requirements and geopolitical/trade uncertainties affecting market access, margins and predictability of export-oriented businesses; India's price-control mechanisms for essential medicines can additionally pressure margins and investment decisions.
risks.risk: Global pricing, market-access and affordability pressures
